newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi TV shows men admitting murder of Jordanian driver.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi TV shows men admitting murder of Jordanian driver.

text.p: Iraqi television on Saturday showed a Saudi and a Jordanian man who confessed to the killing in November of a Jordanian embassy driver on the desert highway between Baghdad and Amman.

Zeban Battah Hdaij al-Rowaili, 27, a Saudi national and Nasr Hantour al-Rowaili, 24, a Jordanian, appeared on television and explained how they, with a third Syrian suspect on the run, Tarrad al-Halabi, killed the Jordanian driver Omar Ahmed Ali al-Subh and stole his car.
They said they killed al-Subh while he was driving the embassy's diplomatic car on the desert highway between Baghdad and the Jordanian border.

"We saw him filling his car with fuel on the highway and we followed him...We stopped him 12 km (seven miles) from the petrol station and asked him to leave the car, he refused and I fired three bullets at him and he was killed," al-Rowaili said.
He said he and his friends worked in smuggling and moved between Saudi Arabia, Syria, Jordan and Lebanon.
The head of the Iraqi Police Department Major-General Tahir Jalil al-Haboush said on television the three entered Iraq illegally using a car with a Saudi registration plate number.
Nasr al-Rowaili said they found a diplomatic bag containing documents which they burned before fleeing to Syria with the Jordanian car.
Haboush said police caught the two after returning back to Iraq from Syria in December.
In January Iraq announced that it had arrested the two and urged the Syrian authorities to try to arrest al-Halabi.
Soon after the killing in November, the Jordanian Foreign Ministry summoned Iraq's ambassador to Jordan and held the Iraqi government responsible for the shooting.
